recognize_zh: 血液抹片中有大量大小不一的微小球形紅血球與紅血球碎片、出芽狀紅血球（放大小圖），血球分析儀的 PLT-O 與 RET 散佈圖在低前向散射區出現異常群（紅圈、箭頭），代表碎片被誤算為血小板，符合熱傷害造成的後天性熱變性異形紅血球症。
features: Panel A: marked anisopoikilocytosis with numerous microspherocytes and tiny red cell fragments (microfragments) of platelet size
Insets: red cells with budding protrusions, spherocytic fragments and irregular dense forms
Panel B: RBC histogram with a main peak plus a left-sided shoulder/tail from small particles
Panel C: PLT impedance histogram with a right tail not returning to baseline, suggesting interfering small red cells
Panels E-F: PLT-O and RET scattergrams showing an abnormal population in the low forward-scatter region (red circles/arrows) representing red cell fragments
Panel D: PLT-F (fluorescent platelet) scattergram used as the reference count, less affected by fragments
describe_en: Composite of a peripheral blood smear and hematology analyzer output. The smear shows marked anisopoikilocytosis with abundant microspherocytes, budding red cells and platelet-sized red cell microfragments, with scattered normal-appearing platelets and a leukocyte. The analyzer histograms and scattergrams show an abnormal small-particle population in the low forward-scatter region of the optical platelet and reticulocyte channels (circled), indicating that red cell fragments interfere with optical/impedance platelet counts, whereas the fluorescent platelet channel is more reliable. Findings are consistent with acquired thermal-injury ('pyro') poikilocytosis, such as after extensive burns, resembling hereditary pyropoikilocytosis.

ddx.vs: Similar microspherocytes and fragments but lifelong, with elliptocytes in family members, spectrin defects and extremely low MCV without burn history.
Schistocytes are helmet and triangular forms with severe thrombocytopenia, rather than round microspherocytes and budding cells with a normal fluorescent platelet count.
Spherocytes are of more uniform size without abundant microfragments or budding, with positive DAT in immune cases or EMA-binding defect in HS.
